ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Korea AML/CFT Act), Act on Regulation of Specified Financial Transactions, Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations implemented via the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) Guidelines, and the Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act (Sangbeop) requiring shareholder registers and ultimate beneficial owner identification under the Act on Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (substantive law: Commercial Act Article 289, issued by the court registrar)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Court Registry Office (Beopmubucheong Court Registration Bureau)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issue original Korean-language Certificate of Incorporation at the court registry, then authenticate by apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) under the Hague Apostille Convention (Korea acceded 1995); no consular legalization should be chained after apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (commercial registration certificate with no pending dissolution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Court Registry Office (Beopmubucheong Court Registration Bureau)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Request the Certificate of Good Standing directly from the registry; for cross-border use, attach apostille issued by MOFA; for use in a non-Hague state, use consular legalization alone after signature authentication by MOFA and then the consulate of the receiving state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the local licensed attorney (statutory corporate filing agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chusik Hoesa board (issued at the registered office in Korea) and notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague states: notarization in Korea followed by apostille by MOFA; for non-Hague states: notarization, authentication by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalization at the consulate of the target jurisdiction; never both apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jeong-gwan) reflecting the panel-survey platform purpose and authorized share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The incorporators of the Chusik Hoesa and the court registration office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled version issued by MOFA for Hague-member destination; for non-member destination, consular legalization through the destination embassy in Seoul with prior MOFA attestation. The authentication path will be selected exclusively based on the counterparty country's status under the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter in English from a Korean commercial bank evidencing the intended local bank account and corporate solvency pre-screening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean commercial bank branch where the pre-incorporation deposit or corporate account reservation is held
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use abroad as evidence of banking status: bank seal and signature notarized, then apostille by MOFA if the receiving state is an Apostille Party; otherwise consular legalization by the consulate of the receiving state; extraction of customer due diligence documents maintained by KoFIU is not included in the notarial bundle.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The Korean financial intelligence unit requires all entities engaging in market research and cross-border payout activities to screen each shareholder, director, beneficial owner, and counterparty bank against the United Nations Security Council sanctions list, the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the EU consolidated sanctions lists, and Korea's own domestic restricted persons list developed under the Financial Transactions Reports Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. In addition, every individual holding more than 25 percent, whether directly or through nominee chains, must be subjected to enhanced continuous transaction monitoring and negative news screening for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including domestic ministerial PEPs and foreign PEPs, using a risk-based approach. The screening results must be logged, timestamped, and retained for at least five years and reported immediately to KoFIU upon any positive match, with a full written policy governing false-positive handling, customer risk rating at low risk, rescreening every six months, and pre-incorporation verification of the identity documents and source-of-funds declarations of all non-resident UBOs.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: In the Republic of Korea, pre-incorporation name clearance is performed via the Court Registration Information portal (Beop-woo, iros.go.kr) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea, with the official corporate name search and protection database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Korean Commercial Act requires every Chusik Hoesa name to be written in Hangeul script in the commercial register. No English-only legal name is permitted for domestic registration. When the company will transact internationally, the Hangeul name may be accompanied by a registered phonetic transliteration in English or other Romanized characters, but the statutory name remains Hangeul. For foreign UBOs, the English name is transliterated using the Revised Romanization of Korean for the corporate name, while personal names are rendered in the original passport Latin alphabet only as an alias in the shareholder register. Four-tier naming conventions are required: (1) the Hangeul corporate distinctive name, (2) the business-purpose descriptor reflecting consumer polling and market research, (3) the company type suffix 'chusik hoesa' or 'Chusik Hoesa' used abridged, and (4) the Korean registration number and English name for tax invoices. Since the proposed ISIC 7320 activity is not a licensed financial or legal profession, no statutory approval from a ministry is required for the name descriptor.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed Hangeul corporate name, the incorporator must submit a written administrative appeal within seven judicial days to the local court registration office, specifying the exact grounds of rejection, showing original search results from the Supreme Court portal, and proposing a distinct alternative name with documentary evidence that the existing identical or similarly confusing name cannot be used. The court will review against the Commercial Act and the Registration of Commercial Names Rules. If rejected again, the company may file a corrective application with the same registry office or appeal to the Supreme Court of Korea within fourteen days. All notices must be in Hangeul, and the appeal should be accompanied by notarized authorization from any non-resident UBO so that the Korean attorney can represent the applicant.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally impermissible as the registered seat of a Chusik Hoesa for the consumer survey platform because the Korean Commercial Act requires an actual physical place of business within the jurisdictional court's territorial district where statutory notices, books, and employee contracts can be inspected. The National Tax Service and commercial banks will require a physically signed lease agreement or full ownership title. However, a stable subleased serviced-office suite with a physical meeting room, dedicated postal receiving facility, and a full-time local office attendant may satisfy the registered-office requirement, provided the underlying lease is for at least one year and the business registry is notified. Co-working membership cards alone, PO boxes, or digital mailrooms are rejected by banks for the receipt of PayPal Mass Payout and Wise settlement proceeds because the foreign payment processor's customer due diligence will demand proof of a physical establishment. The tax office will additionally require that all books, invoices, and employment records are accessible at that address on business days.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection likelihood: high, rated 70 percent likelihood, for a newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa in the Seoul High Court registration district because the Seoul Metropolitan Government and the National Tax Service conduct random presence checks on newly registered companies and corporate address providers. Checklist for inspection: (1) office or serviced suite physically accessible during business hours with a sign bearing the registered Hangeul company name; (2) a permanent on-site mailbox with the exact registered business address; (3) valid lease agreement and utility bills matching the registration; (4) business cards and commercial invoices displaying the same office address; (5) no evidence of mailbox-only arrangements such as low-quality photos or shared PO boxes; (6) local employee or director-owner available to receive process service; (7) the company's corporate seal and registered certificates kept at the address; (8) banking and payroll records sufficient to show operating substance. If deemed inactive at four visits, the NTS may void the business registration, impose a fine, or issue a tax residence challenge. The likely ratio of announced to unannounced inspections is 20 percent announced, 80 percent unannounced, so every day must be inspection-ready.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary fee table, once for all incorporation documents, about KRW 850,000.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as most recently amended by Act No. 17935), especially Articles 288 through 317 on incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa, Article 295 on deposit of subscription price, Article 329(4) on absence of minimum capital, and Article 330 on par value; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559, as amended), Article 5; Local Tax Act (Act No. 17936), Article 29 on registration tax; and the Registration of Real Estate and Corporate Registration Rules of the Supreme Court.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the entity, in standard cases the Civil Registry Division of the Seoul Central District Court for a Seoul office, using the i-ROIS electronic registration system; separate tax registration with the District Tax Office of the National Tax Service under Hometax.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (Chusik Hoesa) under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, accompanied by notarized Articles of Incorporation, certificate of payment of subscription price, director and auditor appointment documents, and statutory minutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under Article 329(4) of the Commercial Act there is no statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Chusik Hoesa; the amount is fixed freely in the Articles of Incorporation. The full subscription price must, however, be deposited in cash at a bank or financial institution before registration under Article 295, and the bank's certificate of subscription payment is mandatory evidence for the registration court. No blocked escrow account is required specifically for incorporation, but funds remitted from abroad by non-resident investors may require a Foreign Investment Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before the deposit is accepted by a foreign exchange bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned individuals, being all of the directors of KR_CHUSIKHOESA, a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) duly organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea, and having been elected at the constitutive general shareholders meeting, hereby adopt the following resolutions pursuant to the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation. 1. Share Capital Subscription. RESOLVED, that the issued share capital of the company shall be [Z] common shares, each with par value of KRW [Y], fully subscribed and paid in cash by the initial shareholders in accordance with Article 295 of the Commercial Act; that the share subscription list, the bank payment certificate, and the register of shareholders are approved in their present form; that the registered capital and any share premium shall be recorded accurately in the capital ledger; and that the directors are instructed to maintain all statutory share records. 2. Banking Authorization. RESOLVED, that the Representative Director is authorized to open, operate, and close bank accounts in the name of the company at such Korean or foreign banking institutions as may be appropriate; that any such bank may rely on a certified copy of this resolution until written revocation is delivered to the bank; that the Representative Director alone, or the Representative Director jointly with the CFO as banking protocols require, shall have signing authority; and that such authority includes domestic and foreign currency accounts, electronic banking, payment gateway settlement, PayPal Mass Payout accounts, and Wise payment rails. 3. Registered Office. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company is adopted and fixed at [full street address], Republic of Korea, within the registration jurisdiction of the [District Court]; that such registered office shall be used for statutory service, notices, court filings, tax registration, and corporate records; and that the Representative Director is authorized to execute a lease, obtain the landlord's registration consent, and file any location-related notices. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed and continues as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer of the company, and that [Name] is appointed as Auditor (or member of the Audit Committee, as applicable), each to serve until the next ordinary general shareholders meeting in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation; and that such officers accept their statutory duties, including preparation of annual financial statements, internal control, and exercise of independent oversight. 5. Implementation. RESOLVED, that the Representative Director and legal counsel are jointly authorized to complete the corporate registration, business registration with the National Tax Service, foreign investment reporting, payroll setup, industrial accident insurance filing, data protection registrations, and all ancillary or incidental filings necessary to make the company fully operational; and that all resolutions are effective upon the completion of incorporation registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarial Certification of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public commissioned under the Notary Act of the Republic of Korea, typically at a notary office located in Seoul or the province where the registered office will sit.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation of the Chusik Hoesa in accordance with Commercial Act Articles 289 through 292. The draft must state the corporate name, business purpose covering consumer polling, cross-border market research, SaaS platform operation, data analytics, management consultation, and all lawful ancillary activities; the maximum number of authorized shares; par value; issue price; total authorized capital; the address of the registered office in Korea; publicity method; and the names and identification details of the incorporators. Once the final text is approved by the shareholders and legal counsel, all incorporators must appear before a Korean notary public, sign or seal the articles in the notary's presence, and obtain a notarial certificate. This record is a mandatory prerequisite for the subsequent court registration and for the bank's opening of a paid-in capital holding account.
required_dossiers: Passport or foreign corporate certificate of each incorporator
Power of attorney for counsel if signed remotely
Final Korean-language Articles of Incorporation in notarization form
Share subscription schedule listing shareholder names and share counts
Directors and auditor appointment consents
Certificate of corporate seal impression if a corporate seal is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a discrepancy between the business purpose and the proposed activities, amend the articles and re-execute the notarization within one business day. If the identity verification of a foreign incorporator fails, obtain an apostilled passport or notarized foreign corporate extract and resubmit the same notarial file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription Payment and Bank Depository Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial institution in the Republic of Korea with foreign exchange dealing authority, such as Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank, or Hana Bank, acting as the depository for subscription payments under Commercial Act Article 295.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary incorporation deposit account in the name of the company or the incorporators, and ensure that every subscriber transfers the full cash subscription price for the shares subscribed. The bank must issue a formal certificate of payment of subscription price or an equivalent deposit certificate stating the corporate name, amount deposited, account name, and date. For non-resident investors, the inward remittance should be routed through a bank authorized to handle foreign exchange transactions, and the remitter's identity and source of funds must be documented. Do not proceed to court registration unless the bank certificate confirms that the aggregate amount matches the total subscription price stated in the articles.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Share subscription list
Passport of each subscriber or corporate certificate of corporate investors
Foreign exchange transaction declarations for foreign remittances
Bank account opening application and customer due diligence forms
Power of attorney for account signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires a Foreign Investment Report before accepting a non-resident investor's remittance, complete the KOTRA or designated bank reporting first and then resubmit the wire. If the amount on the bank certificate is incorrect, request the bank to issue a corrected certificate before taking the registration file to court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration of Incorporation of the Chusik Hoesa
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Registration Section of the Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office, using the Supreme Court electronic registration portal i-ROIS or in-person filing at the court registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company along with all statutory exhibits to the registration court. The court will examine whether the incorporation procedures were lawful, including whether the Articles of Incorporation were notarized, whether the share capital was fully paid and deposited, whether the officers consented, and whether the registered office is identifiable and validly leased. The court will then enter the company into the corporate register and issue a Certificate of Corporate Registration. The filing party must verify the accurate spelling of the corporate name in Korean and English, the registry number, the registered office address, the authorized capital, and the appointed Representative Director before accepting the certificate.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of payment of subscription price
Report of directors and auditor appointment
Written consent or acceptance letter from each director and auditor
Register of shareholders or subscriber list
Power of attorney if filing is done by counsel
Court registration fee and registration tax payment forms
Lease agreement and landlord's consent for the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplementary order, submit all requested documents within the period stated, generally two weeks, through the same registration portal. If the application is rejected, correct the omission, pay any additional fee, and file a fresh application immediately, or file an appeal against the rejection in accordance with non-contentious civil procedure rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea having jurisdiction over the company's registered office, with e-filing through the Hometax portal at www.hometax.go.kr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days after incorporation, file the Application for Business Registration with the competent District Tax Office. The National Tax Service will assign the corporate tax, VAT, and employment withholding registrations to the company and issue a Business Registration Certificate. The application should state the corporate legal form, registered office, representative director, main business code matching ISIC 7320 market research, startup date, and expected business activities. For cross-border SaaS and market research services, legal counsel should simultaneously review whether exports are zero-rated for VAT and whether a foreign investor is eligible for tax incentives. The certificate must be obtained before issuing tax invoices, hiring employees in Korea, or opening operating bank accounts that require tax registration.
required_dossiers: Application for Business Registration in prescribed NTS form
Certificate of Corporate Registration from the District Court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Lease agreement and confirmation of business place
Photo ID or passport copy of the Representative Director
Power of attorney for tax representative if filed through an accountant
Copies of bank account information if electronic tax invoices will be issued
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office flags a mismatch between the registered office and the lease, obtain a corrected lease or landlord confirmation and resubmit within the NTS notice period. If the business code is questioned, provide a written scope description showing that the platform is a market research and consumer polling SaaS business, and not an unlicensed financial activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Report and Cross-Border Capital Filing (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: KOTRA Invest Korea Foreign Investment Support Center and designated foreign exchange banks, with jurisdiction under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Where any non-resident shareholder subscribes shares in the Chusik Hoesa, the shareholder or the company must file a Foreign Investment Report with KOTRA or through a designated foreign exchange bank before the capital is contributed or promptly after the contract is concluded. The report sets out the foreign investor's identity, investment amount, share acquisition method, and purpose. KOTRA will issue a Foreign Investment Notification Certificate, which is required for subsequent visa matters, capital account operations, future dividend repatriation, and certain tax incentives. Even if no foreign investment applies, counsel should ensure that the initial share capital remittance is declared under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. This filing should be coordinated with the bank used in Step 2 so that the paid-in capital certificate remains consistent.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Report form prescribed by KOTRA or the bank
Passport copy of the foreign investor
Certificate of incorporation of the foreign corporate shareholder if applicable
Power of attorney for local counsel
Copy of the share subscription agreement or articles
Bank wire confirmation and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KOTRA or the foreign exchange bank requests corporate records of the foreign investor, provide an apostilled or consular-certified certificate of existence from the investor's home jurisdiction. If the report is rejected because the investment amount falls below statutory thresholds, file the simplified capital transaction declaration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act instead.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. ISIC 7320 consumer panel survey platform is classified as digital market research and SaaS; no industrial licensing board, municipal factory license, chemical licensing authority, or manufacturing permit is required for the pure digital/consulting operational model.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. The entity is not conducting physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing under ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx, so no industrial operating license is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea has no mandatory EIA role for a non-physical, non-construction market research platform.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Exempt. The activity does not fall under any project category listed in Article 2 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and its Enforcement Decree, so no Full EIA Report, Preliminary Environmental Review, or Environmental Registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The operation generates no regulated wastewater, VOCs, atmospheric emissions, or hazardous waste streams. General office waste and end-of-life IT equipment must be disposed of in accordance with the Waste Management Act and the Act on Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources; any devices containing personal data must be sanitized before disposal in compliance with the Personal Information Protection Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a non-manufacturing digital office. No Civil Defense fire permit is mandated. The company must still comply with general workplace safety obligations: enroll all employees in the four major social insurances including Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance with the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service, and ensure the ordinary office meets fire-safety facility standards under the Fire Facilities Installation, Maintenance and Safety Management Act. A standard office business license is sufficient; no additional occupational clearance certificate is required for market research software operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic tax portal (www.hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS for export clearance
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After incorporation of a Korean Chusik Hoesa, the entity must register with the National Tax Service and obtain a 10-digit business registration number, which functions as both the corporate TIN and the VAT registration number. The statutory procedure is as follows: (1) complete the Korean incorporation and corporate registry process including the articles of incorporation and appointment of a representative director; (2) obtain the official certificate of corporate registry and evidence of the domestic place of business; (3) hold a board or shareholder resolution authorizing the person or firm that will sign and file the tax registration; (4) file the business registration application with the NTS district tax office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business, in accordance with the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act, within 20 days of business commencement; (5) if the foreign owner or director is a foreign non-resident entity, appoint a domestic tax representative to receive service, file returns, pay tax, and receive refunds, and attach the tax representative's written authorization to the registration filing; (6) the NTS will then issue the business registration certificate and assign the business registration number through HomeTax. A foreign non-resident entity that makes a taxable supply in Korea outside the registered Chusik Hoesa, or through a Korean permanent establishment, must independently complete VAT registration using the same domestic tax representative procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not operate a check-the-box or elective pass-through regime for Chusik Hoesa corporations. Corporate income tax is imposed at entity level under the Corporate Income Tax Act, the simplified taxpayer regime under the VAT Act is not available to a Chusik Hoesa, and hybrid mismatch adjustments are applied mandatorily under Korean tax law without any entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold applies to a Chusik Hoesa; VAT registration is mandatory for any profit-seeking business operator from business commencement. For non-corporate individual suppliers only, the VAT Act provides a simplified taxpayer regime when annual taxable turnover is below KRW 80,000,000 for services, but this simplified threshold is unavailable to a Chusik Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax e-tax invoice system. The electronic tax invoice must be transmitted to NTS by the day following issuance, and the system performs automatic validation of the counterparty's business registration number, invoice fields, supply value, VAT amount, zero-rated supply value, and dates. Integrated ERP/API submission is permitted, and the NTS e-invoice system is the anti-fraud control layer; there is no separate fiscal printer or physical digital stamping regime. Export declarations are processed through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS in real-time, and the NTS cross-matches export invoice data with customs clearance and foreign exchange settlement data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods qualifies for zero-rating under the Value-Added Tax Act when the goods are moved out of Korea under a Korea Customs Service export declaration and the export price is received in foreign currency by a Korean foreign exchange bank. Qualifying offshore digital services, including market research and consumer panel survey SaaS, are zero-rated when the recipient is a foreign non-resident and the place of supply and actual place of use and consumption is outside Korea, evidenced by the recipient's business location, service agreement, and usage records. The zero-rating remains conditional on actual collection of the foreign exchange consideration within the statutory repatriation period; failure to collect within the period causes the supply to be recharacterized as taxable and subject to retrospective VAT assessment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration (Export Customs Clearance record on Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement out of Korea
Commercial Invoice and supply contract or purchase order with the foreign customer
Packing list and export-related transport documents
Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank, equivalent to an inward remittance certificate
Electronic tax invoice reflecting the zero-rated export supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may deny export zero-rating and claw back the full 10% VAT if the export fact, foreign exchange receipt, or qualifying documentation is not substantiated. Retroactive corrective assessments apply to the original VAT return period, plus daily statutory late-payment interest. Negligent underreporting is subject to an additional tax of 10% of the underpaid VAT, rising to 40% for fraudulent or intentional underreporting. False or forged export declarations and false electronic tax invoices are referred under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying criminal sanctions, fines, confiscation of illegally claimed VAT refunds, disqualification from the export VAT refund system, and joint liability for corporate representatives and related persons.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (with supplementary regulatory oversight and policy formulation by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Foreign Exchange Information Network)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized exchange control system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is officially classified as freely convertible in the current account for trade of goods and services; however, actual settlement is administered through authorized foreign exchange banks and subject to document-based reporting to the Bank of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance. For capital account movements, the regime shifts from a negative-list notification framework to a prior-approval framework for particularly sensitive operations such as short-term offshore borrowing, Korean won cross-border deposits, and derivative transactions exceeding regulatory de minimis thresholds. Export proceeds are generally credited to foreign currency accounts and must be reported within the statutory declaration window; effectively, funds can be retained in U.S. dollars or other usable currencies for treasury management, but conversion into KRW for operational disbursements requires declaration of the underlying cross-border transaction. Profit remittances by a foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa require a remittance report together with audited financials, tax payment certificates, and evidence of the paying commercial purpose; the Bank of Korea concurrently monitors large remittances through the Electronic Foreign Exchange Information System. In practice, current account payment to foreign market-research panelists is openly permissible, while intercompany capital repayment or dividend outflow must meet the substance-plus-documentation test. The practical barrier is not the absence of convertibility but the mandatory declaration and the need for a mainstream domestic bank account as the corridor for KRW clearing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 23 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the delegated Foreign Exchange Transaction Rules, a Korean resident exporter is required to collect and repatriate export-related foreign currency proceeds within the settlement maturity of the underlying contract, generally not exceeding 180 days from the date of export declaration or service completion, unless an extension is granted by the Ministry of Economy and Finance. The current regime imposes a zero mandatory conversion ratio to Korean won; export receipts may be held 100% in an authorized domestic foreign currency current account. Once the proceeds are credited, the exporter must notify the foreign exchange bank and complete the settlement reporting through the Foreign Exchange Information Network; if the treasurer chooses to convert the received currency into KRW, conversion is executed at the prevailing spot rate and must be accompanied by the relevant commercial purpose declaration. A failure to meet the 180-day collection timeline without obtaining an approved extension exposes the company to administrative penalties under the FETA enforcement decree.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD multi-currency current account)
Capital Escrow Account and Operating Settlement Account
Foreign Exchange and Trade Settlement Current Account
Corporate Basic Account with FX Remittance Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally restricted in South Korea. Non-bank fintech EMIs, including global digital EMI brands such as Wise or Revolut Business, may not independently issue Korean won settlement accounts or function as the primary corporate bank for a KR-licensed Chusik Hoesa. The Banking Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act reserve demand deposit-taking and FX inward remittance services for authorized banks. A foreign EMI can only act as a complementary payout channel for lower-value cross-border panelist allowances, typically via a licensed partner-bank sponsored solution; the counterparty bank may require the same CDD and KYC evidence as the domestic tier-1 institution. The onboarding team should therefore plan for a local branch account as the clearing anchor and use the EMI solely for micro-disbursement aggregation. High-risk or unlicensed EMIs that are not registered under the Korean foreign exchange bank framework cannot be legally used for any FX settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A Korean branch-level physical presence or an authenticated in-branch interview is generally mandatory for the statutory director or ultimate shareholder when opening the corporate account, particularly where the shareholder is a non-resident. Remote opening is usually unavailable at the most conservative first onboarding stage. Acceptable alternatives include (1) personal attendance by the director at the designated branch of Shinhan, KB, Hana, or Woori, or (2) a notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney nominating a Korean resident director or senior officer to appear in person, accompanied by the original corporate seal certificate and certified copies of the directors' passports. A consular proxy opening without a domestic POA is not accepted in mainstream tier-1 banks because the CDD interview must verify the signatory against the bank's live sanction-screen and source-of-funds checks. For a foreign-remote director, the practical route is to route account opening through the bank's overseas subsidiary and then request a local branch review, but physical attendance at the Korean branch at least once remains the safest compliance assumption.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO with an opaque intermediate holding structure, causing the Korean bank to fail to understand the ultimate economic activity of the survey platform's revenues.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A consolidated group ownership chart showing the natural persons holding more than 25%; certified passports with apostilles; the founding charter of the Chusik Hoesa; the outside-in registry extract from the Korean Supreme Court / court registry; a signed UBO declaration on the bank's prescribed form; and three months of entity bank statements proving the market research business flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds ambiguity for the initial paid-in capital, especially if the sponsor wires from a high-risk jurisdiction or a personal account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT and bank letters confirming the remitting account holder; the sponsor's personal net-worth statement and tax filings; audited financial statements of the investor entity; the subscription agreement or capital injection resolution; the Foreign Investment Report / declaration filed with the Ministry of Economy and Finance or KOTRA, if applicable; and a detailed market research SaaS revenue forecast explaining the commercial justification for capital raising.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Screening and PEP/Sanctions hits on a director, shareholder, or panel-payout beneficiary, which may arise from common Korean name transliterations or from payouts to consumer survey participants in sanctioned countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A vendor-generated AML/sanction screening report (e.g., Dow Jones, LexisNexis, Refinitiv World-Check) with match reconciliation; certified identification documents; explanation letters for each hit; passport-side spelling variations; proof that the beneficiary is a natural-person panelist with no commercial tie to the sanctioned entity; and a board-approved negative-news resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expedited or split payment patterns to foreign panelists for a market research platform, which can be viewed by the bank as potential money-mule layering if not fully documented.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The executed research participation agreement for a sample panelist; the public survey questionnaire and compensation schedule; a customer-consent privacy policy; panelist identity verification records for new respondents; a treasury policy library with the monthly payout batch concept; and a proof that the payouts correspond to completed, timestamped fieldwork responses.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection into the Chusik Hoesa should be routed through a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank by means of a SWIFT MT103 wire from the investor's account, with the wire field 70 message clearly labeled 'Foreign Direct Investment Capital Injection for KR_CHUSIKHOESA under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act'. Before remittance, the company should notify the bank using the Foreign Currency Payment Request form and complete the Foreign Investment Report online through Korea's Foreign Investment Support System or with the MOEF/KOTRA if the equity share exceeds the statutory notification threshold. The bank will credit the temporary escrowed capital account to verify the purpose code and source of funds. Once payment is confirmed and the board-resolution verification is passed, the funds are reclassified to paid-in capital and a capital verification certificate is issued under the Korean Commercial Act. The treasury team must retain the SWIFT certificate, the bank's foreign exchange transaction confirmation, the share issuance resolution, and the final paid-in-capital ledger entry to support later dividends or liquidation proceeds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For disbursements to overseas panel-sampling participants and research vendors, the main clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 export-of-service trade remittance from the Chusik Hoesa's Korean current account to the beneficiary's account, with the Bank of Korea's trade purpose code for professional, scientific, and technical activities. The bank will require a standard invoice, a statement of contractual service performance, and, when the remittance exceeds the bank's de minimis threshold, an electronic declaration via the Foreign Exchange Information Network. For larger research-vendor contracts, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit can be used as a settlement instrument, but LC terms in services typically depend upon documentary proof of platform usage rather than shipping documents; Documentary Collections may be used only for supported physical deliverables such as hardware survey-device procurement. Standing treasury instructions should split batches of panelist payouts into aggregated ACH sweeps within Korea, while foreign users receive via the selected foreign bank correspondent clearing network through the SWIFT MT103 spine, ordinarily on same-day T+1 value dating. Each outbound instruction must include the proper remittance information fields (beneficiary name, payment reference, and tax identification) to ensure the remittance is not rejected for insufficient purpose-code detail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore Korean won forwards for verified current-account trade exposures offered by tier-1 Korean banks, with the underlying invoice and survey-service contract required.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) transactions in Korean won executed with Deutsche Bank, HSBC, Citi, or approved Korean bank dealing rooms, subject to the regulatory admissible underlying test under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
Straightforward FX spot conversion for operations only, when no hedge is needed.

Plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps (KRW vs USD) for long-term syndicated debt or dividend planning, provided the derivative is contractually linked to the actual liability or cash-flow stream and documented in the annual FX forward position report.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, retained earnings statement and notes) under the Korean Commercial Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local District Court Registry (Registration Division, Court of Law) with jurisdiction over the company's principal office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 calendar days after the ordinary meeting of shareholders. The meeting must be convened no later than 3 months after the close of the fiscal year (for a December 31 year-end: by March 31; filing by April 7).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 5 million (approx. USD 3,800) imposed by the court; if the financial statements are not filed for two consecutive years and the company has no registered business activity, the court may issue an ex officio dissolution order (administrative strike-off) under Article 176 of the Commercial Act, after which the company's registration is struck from the corporate register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (including taxable income and profit reconciliation schedules, with accompanying audited financial statements when applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), through the district tax office or Hometax online system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end: March 31 of the following year; if the company's tax base is computed by a certified tax accountant, an automatic one-month extension to April 30 is allowed; further extension not exceeding 30 days is available on a discretionary basis.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid corporate tax accrues daily interest of 0.022% (approx. 8.03% annual); underreporting penalty of 10% of the additional tax due or 30% for filing failure; if a company is dormant and fails to file for 5 consecutive years, the NTS may recommend judicial dissolution or a strike-off of the commercial registration to the court, and will revoke the business tax registration thereby making the entity administratively defunct.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax (provincial/metropolitan corporate surtax) annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (Si/Gun/Gu) via the Wetax local tax e-filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same calendar deadline as the national corporate income tax return: March 31 for the preceding fiscal year (December 31 year-end); extended to April 30 when national filing is extended.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquent local income tax is subject to a 20% negligence penalty and a daily late-payment interest of 0.075% from the day after the statutory deadline; prolonged non-payment triggers compulsory property collection and registration of the taxpayer as a chronic delinquent, but the administrative strike-off of the corporation itself follows the national tax noncompliance path.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Chusik Hoesa must appoint a licensed independent CPA auditor for each fiscal year if any one of the following tests is met at fiscal year-end: (i) total assets of at least KRW 5 billion (approx. USD 3.85 million); (ii) annual revenue of at least KRW 10 billion (approx. USD 7.7 million); (iii) average number of employees of at least 100 (including full-time equivalents); (iv) total liabilities of at least KRW 5 billion; (v) the company is a listed issuer, a financial institution, or has issued public securities to 100 or more investors; or (vi) the company is specifically ordered by the Financial Services Commission to undergo an audit. Even if these thresholds are not met, the National Tax Service may require audited financial statements where the taxpayer claims repatriation of a corporate income tax refund exceeding KRW 2 billion or applies for certain research and development tax credits.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as enacted in the Republic of Korea, or the general Korean GAAP for non-listed business entities (Korean SMEs Accounting Standards / K-GAAP). Tax-basis financial statements must be reconciled to the applicable accounting framework in the statutory corporate tax return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not currently impose a separate annual UBO confirmation filing to the court registry for an ordinary private Chusik Hoesa. The company is obligated to maintain a complete Register of Shareholders and Register of Directors at its registered office. For each share transfer, an endorsement on the share certificate and, where transfer restrictions apply, a board resolution are required; the register must then be updated without undue delay. A 30-day reporting window is triggered only in respect of foreign-exchange filings under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act when a non-resident acquires or changes its holding of 10% or more of total equity with a value exceeding KRW 100 million; such acquisitions must be reported to the foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy within 30 days. Domestically, a transfer of 5% or more of outstanding shares in a non-listed company may require an anti-competition notification to the Korea Fair Trade Commission if the transaction amount exceeds KRW 5 billion (subject to size standards). Additionally, the company must produce its actual beneficial-owner data to the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit within five business days of any AML request. Annual secretarial maintenance requires the registered agent to verify the registers' currency and to trigger the 30-day reports on behalf of foreign shareholders when applicable.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – 25,000 depending on corporate size; for a small ISIC 7320 survey platform, a certified CPA audit engagement in Korea typically ranges from USD 4,000 to USD 12,000, with a review or agreed-upon procedure costing USD 2,500 to USD 6,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 19% standard rate (progressive national brackets 9% / 19% / 21% / 24%, plus 10% local income tax surcharge on national corporate tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones and Specialized Political/Industrial Development Zones can obtain 100% corporate tax reductions for 3 to 5 years and 50% reductions for another 2 years under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Additional incentives include tax credits for new growth source technology facilities, R&D expenses, and wage increase/job creation credits. No patent box regime exists, but R&D tax credits are available under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 110 (Corporate Tax Return) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (HomeTax e-Service).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the return is due by March 31 of the following calendar year. Interim prepayment returns are filed within 2 months of the first half of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Gross Sales and Total Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide business revenue before expenses, including domestic-source and foreign-source income of the Korean company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean Chusik Hoesa owned by foreign shareholders conducting consumer panel surveys, declare every revenue stream including PayPal and Wise settlements from overseas respondents and clients. Cross-border settlement fees or bank charges cannot offset gross revenue; expense treatment is at item level. Omission of foreign-source revenue for a Korean resident entity is treated as unfaithful reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Deductible Expenses and Net Tax Base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary and necessary business expenses, including employee wages, platform hosting, software development, market research, professional fees, depreciation, and royalties paid to related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to foreign related parties must be arm's length and substantiated by contracts. Include all documentation for subcontracted consumer panel data collection, SaaS licensing, and cloud infrastructure. Add back non-deductible entertainment, fines, and any transaction in respect of which transfer pricing documentation has not been maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of progressive corporate income tax rates to the taxable income base, and calculation of the 10% local income tax surcharge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign shareholding percentage does not alter the tax calculation for the Korean entity itself; a Korean-resident company is taxed on worldwide income. Non-resident shareholders must not be treated as exempt merely because they are offshore. After calculating national corporate tax, enter the local income tax surcharge equal to 10% of the national tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits or deductions for foreign income taxes paid on foreign-source income that is also taxable in Korea.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean company earns income from foreign panel surveys and pays withholding or income tax abroad, attach certificates of foreign tax paid. Composite foreign tax credit is limited to Korean tax attributable to the foreign-source income. For related-party arrangements, the credit is denied if the foreign transaction is not recognized at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Non-Resident Shareholder Dividend Withholding Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule identifying dividends distributed, class of shares, foreign shareholder jurisdiction, and tax residence status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean-source dividends paid by the Chusik Hoesa to non-resident corporations are subject to 20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax, i.e. 22% aggregate. Where treaty relief is claimed, attach the Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration. A shareholder possessing more than the treaty ownership threshold must be identified to assess reduced dividend withholding eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of all cross-border transactions with foreign related parties, including sales, royalties, interest, service fees, and cost-sharing arrangements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report every intercompany transaction with foreign affiliates. If aggregate foreign related-party transactions exceed the statutory threshold, attach the Local File and Master File. State the transfer pricing method applied and the FAR analysis (functions, assets, risks). Failure to disclose is a statutory basis for aggravated penalty tax and an anti-abuse adjustment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers an unfaithful filing surcharge of 20% of the unpaid tax, plus daily late-payment interest at the current statutory rate (approximately 0.022% per day) on the overdue amount. Underreporting taxable income by more than one third imposes an underreporting surtax of 10% of the deficient tax, or 20% if the underreporting is intentional. If a return is fraudulently omitted, the National Tax Service can refer the matter for prosecution with imprisonment of directors and fines under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge, resulting in a 22% aggregate statutory withholding rate on outbound dividends paid by a Korean stock corporation to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke the relevant bilateral Double Tax Treaty (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must provide: (1) an original or certified copy of a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the treaty-state competent authority; (2) a beneficial ownership declaration confirming the payee is the actual owner of the shares and the dividend stream; (3) evidence that the dividend is not attributable to a permanent establishment in Korea; and (4) a DTA relief application submitted through the Korean withholding agent or on the NTS HomeTax system before the payment date. The Korean payer must retain the documents. If no TRC is available at payment time, the payer must withhold at the 22% statutory rate and the non-resident may file a domestic refund claim within three years for the excess withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on intellectual property royalties and intercompany debt interest paid by a Korean payer to a non-resident is also 20% national plus 2% local income tax, i.e. 22% aggregate. Treaty rates vary: under many Korean DTAs, interest is reduced to 10-15% and royalties to 10-15% depending on the technology type, copyright bottleneck, or cultural tax regime. The reduced treaty rate is conditional on non-resident beneficial ownership and no connection to a Korean permanent establishment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5 billion per fiscal year in aggregate cross-border related-party transactions (Local File and Master File preparation threshold); Country-by-Country Report filing applies when a multinational group has consolidated revenue of at least KRW 100 billion. This tiered threshold requires contemporaneous records and disclosure of APAs, cost-sharing arrangements, and financial statements.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not apply a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulation, but economic substance remain decisive under the General Anti-Abuse Rule in the National Tax Basic Act, the Korean international tax anti-avoidance framework, and treaty beneficial-ownership jurisprudence. A Korean entity in the cross-border consumer survey SaaS model must demonstrate that core income-generating activities (CIGA) are actually performed in Korea, such as media content creation, panel recruitment, data analytics, board decision-making, and risk management. If the entity is a mere conduit holding trademark or platform rights without Korean staff or decisive control, Korean tax authorities may disregard the shell, disallow treaty benefits, and reallocate income to the beneficial operator.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting online consumer-panel revenue received through PayPal, Wise, Stripe, or crypto rails, or booking such revenue to an offshore affiliate while the Korean company continues to perform all operational functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act imposes criminal liability for fraudulent tax evasion, with penalties of imprisonment for up to 5 years or fines up to 10 times the tax evaded, or both. In addition, the National Tax Service imposes an unfaithful filing penalty of 20% of the underpaid tax plus 0.022% daily interest on the outstanding deficiency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or direct intentionally false returns may be subject to criminal imprisonment. Under Korean Commercial Act Article 401, directors are jointly and severally liable for damages caused to the company by an intentional or negligent violation of the law. Tax authorities can also impose joint liability on directors for taxes when the company is the instrumental tax evasion vehicle, and can issue Personal Tax Clearance certificates or travel blacklists for unpaid national taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Permanent Establishment Peeling
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling consumer survey SaaS services to a foreign related party at a zero-margin or below-cost price, shifting profits to a no-tax jurisdiction, and failing to prepare the required Local File/Master File or to file the International Related-Party Transaction Summary with NTS when the statutory threshold of KRW 5 billion in related-party transactions is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 6 and 7 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs authorize the National Tax Service to disregard or recharacterize transactions, make arm's length redeterminations, and impute income based on deemed functions, assets, and risks. Auditor's adjustments can be assessed as additional corporate tax plus penalty surcharges of 10-20% of underreported tax and daily interest, and a 30% assessment against related non-compliance can be imposed under domestic penalty rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly implement artificial pricing are jointly liable with the company under Commercial Act Article 401. In egregious cases, NTS may hold directors personally for the unpaid deficiency, impose asset-preservation travel bans, and refer executives for criminal prosecutions where a false or fraudulent international tax report was executed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or royalties to a foreign shell shareholder that holds Korean shares only on paper, has no employees, no office, no meaningful assets, and whose sole purpose is to improperly access a reduced DTA rate, without first obtaining a Tax Residency Certificate or beneficial ownership evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean tax authorities may deny treaty relief under the General Anti-Abuse Rule or the Principal Purpose Test introduced through BEPS MLI implementation. The consequences are immediate 22% aggregate withholding assessment on dividends, interest, or royalties, imposition of withholding penalty surcharges, and interest accrual from the original payment date. Filing of fraudulent proprietary forms may also initiate criminal proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who authorizes untaxed dividend repatriation while shielding the beneficial owner is personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax under National Tax Collection Act joint-liability provisions. The director may be blacklisted (travel ban) and unable to perform foreign travel until the deficiency is settled. Where the shell arrangement is designed to commit fraud on the Korean treasury, directors risk up to 5 years' imprisonment and confiscation of personal assets for the evaded tax.
